A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPFSplat and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–12, Figures 1–15 and Appendices A–D. The relocated appendices and references can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report original SPFSplat experiments on novel view synthesis, pose estimation, generalization and component ablations, including quantitative results and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices retain SPFSplat's original quantitative evaluations, ablations and qualitative reconstruction results. These retained experimental outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same shared ViT architecture, Gaussian and pose heads, canonical-space outputs, two training branches and rendering/reprojection losses. The revised efficiency explanation does not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain RE10K, ACID, additional DL3DV training, DTU generalization, mobile-phone photographs and the same overlap and multiple-view scenarios. Appendix relocation introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline membership in Tables 1–4, 8 and 10. This includes the existing adapted MASt3R comparison in the appendix; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The splits, alternative evaluation sets, 256×256 resolution, overlap groups, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, pose-AUC thresholds and predicted-pose versus evaluation-time alignment protocols remain unchanged. Appendix training and multiple-view evaluation settings also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix B retain the same component and loss ablations, pose-supervision experiment, initialization comparisons, training-data and view-count analyses, PnP comparison and failure cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–12 and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SPFSplat's average PSNR 25.484, SSIM 0.847, LPIPS 0.153 and reconstruction time 0.044 seconds under the same setting.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the canonical-space formulation, camera assumptions and rendering, reprojection and auxiliary pose-loss definitions are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about pose-free training and inference, synthesis and pose-estimation performance, efficiency and scalability. Their scientific scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 shifts the efficiency explanation from the shared backbone and lightweight pose head to direct feed-forward Gaussian construction in canonical space. It also explicitly connects PF3plat's pose-estimation overhead to lifting depth predictions into Gaussians. Other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A retain the same initialization, loss weights, hardware, batch size, learning rates and baseline implementation details. The code and trained-model access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 54 works are cited, and Section 2 retains its research positioning and comparisons. The revised runtime discussion preserves the existing contrast with PF3plat; bibliography relocation and updated page backlinks are presentation changes.

P1.justification: The references move from before the appendices to the document's end, while the appendix sequence remains intact. Other edits comprise the short efficiency explanation rewrite and a duplicated-period correction in Appendix C.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive small graphical adjustments, including changing 'Target View' to 'Rendered Target' in Figure 2. Tables 1–2 add rules beneath grouped column headings. Appendix displays relocate with their sections; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The revised efficiency explanation, clearer Figure 2 label and table-formatting adjustments provide light editorial polish. Both versions retain the same method, experimental support, reproducibility information and limitations; the localized refinements do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
